newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares rise on telecoms, lull seen.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares rise on telecoms, lull seen.

text.p: Leading Russian shares rose on Monday, but traders saw average volumes pointing to a possible slowing in the market later in the week despite strong gains in the telecom sector during the day.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index closed at a record 516.63 after closing on Friday at 509.47. Total market turnover was a sturdy $68 million.
"The market needs to calm down a little bit, especially in some shares," said Regent European Securities head of trading Dmitry Starenko, saying a correction had already begun in afternoon trading.

Shares in leading telecoms as well as less liquid shares in telephone companies on the second tier rose by over 10 percent during the day on a wave of investor interest following Friday's sale of a 25 percent stake in holding company Svyazinvest.
Svyazinvest holds controlling interests in 88 regional and other telecoms companies, including Rostelekom, which closed at $5.34 after $4.90 on Friday.
But Rostelekom was off an earlier $5.67 high, and St Petersburg provider PTS closed at $2.80, off a daily high of $2.95 after $2.33 previously.
Moscow city telephone company MGTS closed at $2.35 after Friday's closing $2.03.

"The volatility (in Rostelekom shares) has been quite high -- we saw a rush of interest in the morning but it has backed off since then," said Rinaco Plus trader Tom Brackenbury. "There is still interest in telecoms but it's difficult to say how much."
Other leading Russian shares showed some gains, with national power company UES closing at $0.4280 after $0.4260 previously and savings bank Sberbank ticking up to $313.5 from $303.0.
But a lull which market participants said they had been expecting seemed likely to set in the short term, they said, as the spurt of interest in telecoms slowed.
"This is a turning point -- we will see whether the market will continue growing or whether it will come off a little bit," said Starenko.
